findings.summary: Both retained-UI rules (background under the border, shrink-to-fit beside an absolute offset) were compensated in the projection with a third hand-rolled CSS colour parser, a shorthand tokenizer, a declaration iterator beside two existing ones, a viewport-resolved max-width cap and two write-memos with different undo arms -- ~330 lines that re-parsed every element's style on every tree sync, dirtied RmlUi layout with an unchanged SetProperty, and could not see a border or width authored in a class rule. Altitude named the layer: the pinned RmlUi paints the background over the padding box in ElementBackgroundBorder::GenerateGeometry and GetShrinkToFitWidth forgets the inset that BuildBox subtracts one branch away. Both rules now live in native/patches/rmlui-css-box-model.patch (background over the border box, then the border ring; inset subtracted from the available width), applied by tools/build-rmlui.ps1 beside the rounding patch, and the projection code is deleted.

The physics shim added pair_key, body_entry_of and pair_has_pending_bounce and left the older inline copies standing (two more spellings of the pair key, a second body lookup in the stabilizer, a verbatim copy of the pending-bounce walk as already_scheduled), plus a scan over active_bounces in the stabilizer that was dead because the list is cleared before the stabilizer runs. All routed through the one helper each; the dead scan and the no-op post-swap clear removed.

stepping_world() was a process global set and cleared around the sub-step loop, with two forward declarations to reach it, so the manifold callback could find the world; every collision object in a world is a tracked body, so body_entry_of(object)->world names it. Deleted, with the lookups moved beside the tables.

The rebound carried an A/B role swap (~25 mirrored lines) and ten null-guard ternaries for untracked objects that cannot exist; a static side has zero inverse mass, so Bullet ignores its impulse and contributes nothing to the denominator. Rewritten symmetric in Bullet's own A/B convention, one transform spelling, the null arms replaced by one continue; HavokBounce lost its derivable pair field and the two velocity caches became one BodyVelocity slot cached by member pointer. Every physics number unchanged.

speculative_speed_factor 1.5 and speculative_padding 0.005 were unmeasured constants, and resting_contact_distance 0.02 froze a Bullet default that had silently widened the stabilizer envelope over the manifold's own relative threshold. The threshold is now the derived bound (speed of both bodies plus the sub-step's gravity, over the sub-step -- Bullet integrates gravity before it constrains), never below Bullet's per-pair threshold, and the envelope is that per-pair threshold. Measured identical on scenes 40, 42, 45, 100, 101 and break-meshes; scene 44 moved from 0.005 to 0.006 full (its wall-clock spread is 0.005--0.006 / 0.033--0.037 across runs, gate 0.008/0.045).

Every static body was forced ACTIVE_TAG on its deferred re-add, transform write and impulse (Bullet only ever puts non-static bodies back to sleep), so every pair touching a static ran narrowphase on every sub-step; the explicit-mask addRigidBody overload racer takes also drops Bullet's static-static exclusion. Guarded with isStaticObject() at the three sites and a btOverlapFilterCallback restating Bullet's rule over the authored masks; the per-shape motion disc and breaking threshold are cached at shape creation instead of four virtual bounding-sphere evaluations per manifold per sub-step, inactive pairs skip the refresh, and empty manifolds skip the landing scan.

The stepping model and its measurements were enumerated in five places (the .cpp header essay, docs/fidelity.md, docs/status.md's intro, docs/architecture.md, registry comments) and per-scene residual numbers in four; several registry comments were changelog sentences rather than the gate's rationale. fidelity.md is the one home for mechanism and trajectory numbers; the header comment names the three parts and points there; the status intro, the architecture row, TODO and the registry comments carry pointers and gate purpose.

TODO.md's timer entry claimed racer's countdown runs on wall time, but racer's registry entry sets fixedCaptureEnvironment(); only scene 44 is wall-clock. Corrected, and the three residual classes now each name what unblocks them.

docs/ui.md promised three projected rules and listed two, folded the following paragraph into the list, and embedded a row value (1.208 to 1.309) that verify-status will move. Rewritten for the two patches with a delta.

Box-box pairs keep Bullet's restitution because btBoxBoxDetector emits only penetrating points -- a detector gap, not the Havok last-sub-step edge case fidelity.md gave as the reason; the general mechanism (registerCollisionCreateFunc BOX/BOX onto the convex-convex GJK/EPA algorithm, which honours the threshold) had never been tried.
findings.blockedBy: Tried and measured: routing box pairs through GJK/EPA takes scene 44 from 0.006 / 0.037 to 0.021 / 0.074 (break-meshes unchanged at 0.000), so the box-box detector's contact set is what the stacks rest on. The reason is now stated correctly in fidelity.md with both measurements.

findings.summary: Scene 44's 2000 ms drop runs on the wall clock while the browser harness pins its timers; putting the scene on fixedCaptureEnvironment() would make it deterministic and delete the TODO entry.
findings.blockedBy: Measured: under BBLITE_FRAME_DELTA_MS scene 44 reads 0.337 / 2.202 against 0.005--0.006 on the wall clock, so the native fixed clock does not fire the timeout on the browser's frame (the clock is k*delta in double, so it is the timer-boundary semantics, not accumulation). Aligning it touches every fixed-clock scene that runs timers and wants them re-measured; the scene stays on the wall clock with its spread in the gate.
